newsitem.title: USA: Fox/Liberty buys 40 percent of Rainbow for $850 million.
newsitem.headline: Fox/Liberty buys 40 percent of Rainbow for $850 million.

text.p: In an effort to form a new national sports television venture, Fox/Liberty Networks will pay $850 million for a 40 percent stake in Rainbow Media Holdings Inc.'s sports interests, the companies said on Monday.
Fox/Liberty is a joint venture of News Corp.'s Fox Sports unit and Liberty Media Corp., a unit of Tele-Communications Inc.
As a result of the deal, Fox/Liberty and Rainbow will form a national sports TV programming venture called FOX Sports Net, which is expected to reach 55 million U.S. homes.
Rainbow is 75 percent owned by Cablevision Systems Corp., and 25 percent owned by General Electric Co.'s NBC unit.

The new TV venture, to include national, regional and local sports programming, will appear on nine Fox/Liberty regional cable TV networks, eight Rainbow regional sports channels, and the Fox Sports regional sports systems.
Fox/Liberty said it will fund the $850 million through a bank loan.
